positioning.kit: A user-facing, versioned scaffold that may select one framework adapter.
positioning.adapter: A framework-specific implementation of this contract shared by create and attach flows.
positioning.framework: The owner of agent execution, runtime state, conversations, tools, memory, and orchestration.
positioning.modelProvider: An independently selected model service or local runtime; it is not the framework identity.

workspai: mutation admission and proof-carrying change state
framework: conversation, memory, checkpoint, and runtime state
model invocation and framework-native tool dispatch
channels, schedules, handoffs, and framework telemetry
forbiddenForAdapter: invent or mutate canonical Model or Graph truth
turn inferred framework output into verification evidence
apply source mutations outside the Workspai PCC or Repair admission boundary
persist secrets, unrestricted model output, or absolute machine paths in portable artifacts
overwrite user-authored files without an owned-file or managed-section lease

capabilities.meaning: Run one agent through a declared model and bounded tool surface.
Coordinate multiple named agents without hiding their ownership or handoffs.
Expose tools with machine-validatable input and output contracts.
Load bounded procedures or reusable instructions on demand.
Transfer work between agents with explicit state and responsibility.
Execute a declared graph or ordered workflow rather than an opaque loop.
Stream typed runtime events or model output.
Continue bounded work outside an attached interactive request.
Persist enough runtime state to survive process interruption.
Pause at a declared boundary and resume from an explicit human decision.
Own framework conversation or thread state without becoming workspace truth.
Provide framework memory with explicit scope, persistence, and retention semantics.
Persist resumable workflow checkpoints.
Resume a prior run without silently replaying admitted effects.
Trigger declared work on a schedule.
Receive and send messages through declared external channels.
Consume MCP tools through an explicitly configured client boundary.
Expose framework capabilities through an MCP server boundary.
Emit correlated, redacted runtime telemetry.
Run repeatable agent or workflow evaluations with recorded evidence.
Select among multiple model providers through a stable client boundary.
Use a declared local model provider without claiming offline execution by default.
Run the framework on the user machine.
Run on infrastructure controlled by the user or organization.
Deploy to an upstream or third-party managed runtime.

kitRelationship.rule: An agent project kit declares one primary framework adapter. A workspace may host multiple separately scoped adapter instances, and cross-framework bridges must be explicit. The same adapters are reusable by existing-project attach flows.

versioning.adapterProtocol: SemVer-compatible immutable v1 envelope; breaking fields require v2.
versioning.upstreamFramework: Every adapter declares a bounded supported range and exact tested versions.

stability.experimental: Contract exploration only; not advertised as usable.
stability.preview: Usable only with explicit preview selection and complete required conformance.
stability.stable: All required conformance checks pass on the claimed platform and runtime matrix.
stability.compatibility: Supported for migration or maintained upstream lines; never the default new-project choice.
stability.deprecated: Discovery and migration guidance only; new scaffold is forbidden.

defaults: Network, generated-code execution, secrets, and mutating tools are not implicitly granted.
Framework runtime state is untrusted input to canonical Workspai evidence producers.
All paths are relative, containment-checked, symlink-aware, and bound to an authorized project root.
Portable artifacts contain references or bounded projections, never raw secret-bearing sessions.
Framework dependencies are pinned by a tested-baseline policy and audited before admission.

publication.stableAdmission: A stable adapter requires one passed instance of every required check for each advertised platform/runtime lane and no blockers.
